Biostratigraphy: Vascoceras diartianum portion of Sciponoceras gracile ammonite zone [middle of undifferentiated S. gracile zone (including B. clydense ?); on Meyers et al. (2012) figure]

Locality: Lohali Point section, Blue Gap, Navajo Indian Reservation, Arizona

Locality: Big Sulphur Draw quadrangle, Natrona County, Wyoming

Locality: Burnt Timber Creek, Alberta
Lithostratigraphy: Sunkay Member of Blackstone Fm; 30-cm-thick brownish-gray bentonite enclosed by dark marine mudstone.

Biostratigraphy: Correlated to “X” bentonite of Frontier Fm in Wyoming; therefore coeval with sample 90-O-50 (A. amphibolum ammonite zone). Close to end of regressive phase, just prior to onset of the major transgression culminating in early Turonian most-extensive-flooding of Cretaceous Western Interior basin.

Locality: 12.9 km W of Casper, Wyoming; S. side Wyo Hwy 220
Lithostratigraphy: Top of Mowry Shale; Clay Spur Bentonite

Locality: N. bank Arrow Creek, Judith Basin County, Montana

Locality: Johnson County, Wyoming

Locality: Tengunosaw valley, Hokkaido, Japan
Lithostratigraphy: Hikagenosawa Fm; Yazo Group

Biostratigraphy: “Above FAD of Mantelliceras ammonite” and within range of foraminifer Thalmanninella globotruncanoides.”; however, there is a fault below the sampled horizon, therefore is not reliable for scaling relative to underlying strata (Ando, 2016).

Locality: Tengunosaw valley, Hokkaido, Japan
Lithostratigraphy: Hikagenosawa Fm; Yazo Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Eleven spots on 12 zircon grains.
Zone: Mantelliceras mantelli ammonite zone (base of upper subzone)
Biostratigraphy: Nearly coeval with local FAD of pelagic forminifer Thalmanninella globotuncanoides (primary marker of Albian-Cenomanian boundary).

Locality: Hotei-zawa, Soeushinai area, Hokkaido, Japan
Lithostratigraphy: Upper Bed My3; middle part of Yezo Group

Zone: Mantelliceras mantelli ammonite zone (base of upper subzone)

Locality: Hotei-zawa, Soeushinai area, Hokkaido, Japan

Locality: Kyoei-Sakin-zawa, Soeushinai area, Hokkaido, Japan

Locality: Tengunosaw valley, Hokkaido, Japan
Lithostratigraphy: Hikagenosawa Fm; Yazo Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Seven spots on eleven zircon grains from TNGt001.8 were analyzed by LA-ICPMS.
Biostratigraphy: Above FAD of planktonic foraminifer Pseudothalmanninella subticinensis.

Locality: Gully on N. bank of Peace River, short distance below the “Gates”, British Columbia

Locality: Vöhrum clay pit situated 30 km east of Hannover, 1.6 km SW of Vöhrum, NW Germany

Biostratigraphy: Parahoplites nutfieldiensis ammonite zone [but definition of this zone was not provided in this paper; but see Singer et al. (2015), below for re-analysis of same sample]

Locality: Otto gott clay pit, Sarstedt, 21 km SE of Hannover, Germany
Lithostratigraphy: Trachytic tuff, attributed to the Waddenzee volcanic center located off the Netherlands coast (Mutterlose and Böckel, 1998) within a succession of clays and marls.

Biostratigraphy: Zone is also called “Nolaniceras nolani”. Base of Nolani (hence, top of P. nutfieldiensis Zone) is constrained in Germany by 114.86±0.37 Ar/Ar, which verifies and enhances Obradovich’s 114±1.3 Ma.

Locality: Otto gott clay pit, Sarstedt, 21 km SE of Hannover, Germany
Lithostratigraphy: Trachytic tuff, attributed to the Waddenzee volcanic center located off the Netherlands coast (Mutterlose and Böckel, 1998) within a succession of clays and marls.
Primary radioisotopic age details: Gott K-feldspar sample displays highly reproducible step ages, with a high precision plateau age of 114.85±0.12 Ma, when only analytical uncertainties are considered, using Fish Canyon Tuff age of 28.02 Ma as fluence monitor; not yet converted to new standard of 28.201 Ma (Kuiper et al., 2008)
Zone: lower Acanthohoplites nolani (or slightly above middle of original Parahoplites nutfieldiensis)
Biostratigraphy: Same level as the other Ar/Ar determinations; slightly above middle of original Parahoplites nutfieldiensis

Locality: Bano Nuevo Volcanic Complex, near Cerro Mirador, central Patagonian Cordillera, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: volcanics conformably overlie unconsolidated sands of the Apeleg Fm

Biostratigraphy: upper beds of the Apeleg Formation have been dated as early Aptian based on the presence of the ammonite Tropaeum or Australiceras sp.

Locality: Bano Nuevo Volcanic Complex, near Cerro Mirador, central Patagonian Cordillera, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: volcanics conformably overlie unconsolidated sands of the Apeleg Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of three hornblende 40Ar/39Ar plateau or isochron ages, originally calculated with FCs = 28.02 Ma as the fluence monitor.
Zone: Deshayesites forbesi through E. martinoides zones due to vague biostrat
Biostratigraphy: upper beds of the Apeleg Formation have been dated as early Aptian based on the presence of the ammonite Tropaeum or Australiceras sp.

Locality: Mashenmiao-Zhuanchengzi (MZ) section, Yixian, Liaoning Province, northeast China
Lithostratigraphy: Basalt flows; terrestrial setting
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of three whole rock plateau ages; originally calculated with TCs = 28.34 Ma as the fluence monitor.
Biostratigraphy: No biostratigraphy in this terrestrial section that could be correlated to marine standards. Reversed-magnetization basalt flows (10 samples on transect; no boundaries found to normal polarity). Publication assigned it to be Chron M0r based on the reversed polarity.

Locality: ODP Site 878A (Leg 144), MIT Guyot, western Pacific
Lithostratigraphy: Seamount basalts below transgressive carbonates
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of three whole rock 40Ar/39Ar isochron ages, originally calculated with TCs = 27.92 Ma as the fluence monitor.
Biostratigraphy: MIT seamount normally magnetized (above reversed magnetized), upper hawaiite lavas. Platform carbonates 25 m above volcanic basement are assigned to the lower-Aptian C. litterarius nannofossil biozone (NC6). Implied to be older than mid-Early Aptian

Locality: outcrops along McCarty Creek, 2 miles north of Paskenta, Tehama County, Great Valley, California, USA
Lithostratigraphy: Great Valley Group, California, USA
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of youngest five (of 7) 1–4 grain zircon fractions, utilizing CA-TIMS and in-house UNC spike (0.1% error in tracer calibration), with analytical error expanded in accommodate geologic scatter.
Biostratigraphy: Chiastozygus litterarius biozone (NC6) – Text says NC6A subzone, as supported by the first occurrence of C. litterarius and the last occurrence of Conusphaera rothii in MC887, a sample found below MC888. But, LAD of C. rothii=base subzone 6B, therefore sample is lower NC6B.

Locality: ODP Site 1184 (Leg 192), eastern salient of Ontong Java Plateau, western equatorial Pacific
Lithostratigraphy: Four samples from cores into subunit IIE in the lower part of the volcaniclastic succession.
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 6 (of 8) laser fusions on 4–5 grain aliquots of plagioclase, sampled from four core intervals, originally calibrated to FCs = 28.02 Ma.
Biostratigraphy: The oldest sediment overlying basement on the crest of the Ontong Java Plateau occurs within the upper part of the Leupoldina cabri planktonic foraminiferal zone.

Sample: SG7, SGB25, ML475, KF36, KF53; whole rock basalts
Locality: on-shore sections of Ontong Java Plateau basalts, central Malaita, Solomon Islands; equivalent to OJP basalts drilled in ODP Site 807
Lithostratigraphy: Malaita Volcanic Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 5 whole rock incremental heating plateau ages, originally calculated with FCT-3 biotite=27.55 Ma.
Biostratigraphy: The oldest sediment overlying basement on the crest of the Ontong Java Plateau (ODP sites) occurs within the upper part of the Leupoldina cabri planktonic foraminiferal zone; but there are no biostratigraphic constraints on these Malaita exposures.

Locality: DH-3&7 borehole for U-Pb, DH-2 for C-13 and Magstrat; Svalbard
Lithostratigraphy: Helvetiafjellet Fm; bentonite at 164.4 m depth in DH7 and coeval one in DH3
Primary radioisotopic age details: Midtkandal et al. (2016) merged zircon sets from the same bentonite in two boreholes [DH-3 from Corfu et al. (2013)], and used the 10 youngest zircon grains (of 21).
Biostratigraphy: Indirect palyntology correlations. Lowest meters of overlying Carolinefjellet Formation has a negative then positive C-13 excursion which was interpreted as characteristic of earliest Aptian OAE1a. Position of the ash horizon in adjacent borehole magneostratigraphy indicate it is within mid-Chron M1r (Zhang et al., 2019)

Locality: ODP Site 878 (Leg 144), MIT guyot, western Pacific
Lithostratigraphy: Seamount basalts below transgressive carbonates.
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted average of plagioclase 40Ar/39Ar isochron ages, originally calculated with TCs = 27.92 Ma as the fluence monitor
Zone: Was interpreted as top of M0r; reinterpreted as top M3r
Biostratigraphy: MIT seamount lower alkalic basalts at reversed-upward-to-normal polarity transition; overlain by normal-polarity basalts. Platform carbonates 25 m above volcanic basement are assigned to the lower-Aptian C. litterarius nannofossil biozone (NC6). Implied to be older than mid-Early Aptian. Was interpreted as top of Chron M0r; but re-interpretation might be top of M1r or top of M3r.

Locality: El Porto×n section, Neuquén Basin, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: Interbedded between shales of the upper part of the upper member (Agua de la Mula) of the Agrio Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 6 single zircon grain analyses, utilizing CA-TIMS and the ET535 spike.
Biostratigraphy: Near base of the Sabaudiella riverorum regional ammonite zone

Locality: Neuquén Basin, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: Interbedded between shales of the upper part of the upper member (Agua de la Mula) of the Agrio Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 6 single zircon grain analyses, utilizing CA-TIMS and the ET535 spike.
Biostratigraphy: Within upper part of regional ammonite zone of Paraspiticeras groeberi; which they project to be nearly at end of Hauterivian (uppermost Pseudothurmannia ohmi Zone of Tethyan Mediterranean).

Locality: Neuquén Basin, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: Interbedded between shales of the lowermost part of the upper member (Agua de la Mula) of the Agrio Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 5 single zircon grain analyses, utilizing CA-TIMS and the ET535 spike.
Biostratigraphy: within the Spitidiscus riccardii ammonite zone, correlated with the lower Subsaynella sayni zone of the Tethys

Locality: El Portón section, Neuquén Basin, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: Pilmatué Member of the lower Agrio Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 5 single zircon grain analyses, utilizing CA-TIMS and the ET535 spike.
Biostratigraphy: Base of regional Holcoptychites agrioensis subzone, Holcoptychites neuquensis zone; and they suggest this is approximately coeval to base of Crioiceratites loryi zone of Tethyan Mediteranean. Same level as local highest-occurrence of E. windii nannofossil.

Locality: outcrops along McCarty Creek, 2 miles north of Paskenta, Tehama County, Great Valley, California, USA
Lithostratigraphy: Great Valley Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of youngest eight (of 10) 3–5 grain zircon fractions, utilizing CA-TIMS and in-house UNC spike (0.1% error in tracer calibration), with analytical error expanded in accommodate geologic scatter.
Zone: upper C. oblongata (lower NC3b) nannofossil zone (middle Valanginian)
Biostratigraphy: Calcareous nannofossils of P. fenestrata, R. nebulosus, C. angustiforatus, Cyclagelosphaera deflandrei, Eiffellithus windii, Metadoga mercurius, R. wisei, and Tubodiscus verenae place this sample in the C. oblongata (NC3) biozone – lower E. windii (lower NC3b) subzone

Locality: Kadong section, south side of Yamzho Iyumco Lake, 28.75N, 90.70E, ca. 51km ESE of Nagarze, Tibet.
Lithostratigraphy: Rhyolite is from unit 13 of the upper (volcanic and volcaniclastic) part of Sangxiu Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of fifteen spot analyses analyzed by SHRIMP II (Beijing), using the TEMORA zircon standard
Biostratigraphy: Sample is above a Calcicalathina oblongata–Speetonia colligata assemblage of calcareous nannofossils, but minimum age is unconstrained. Assigned here as Valanginian.

Locality: outcrops along Kelly Road, Paskenta, Tehama County, Great Valley, California, USA
Lithostratigraphy: Great Valley Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of six oldest (of 8) 1–2 grain zircon fractions, utilizing CA-TIMS and in-house UNC spike (0.1% error in tracer calibration).
Zone: lowest C. oblongata (lower NC3a) nannofossil zone (uppermost Berriasian-lowermost Valanginian)
Biostratigraphy: Calcareous nannofossil occurrences suggest correlation to the C. angustiforatus biozone – P. fenestrata subzone (NK-2B) at the oldest, but it is not possible to rule out a younger age with the current biostratigraphy; the sample is conservatively placed at the base of the Valanginian in the lower Calcicalathina oblongata biozone. [C. oblongata begins in lower T. pertransiens ammonite zone]

Locality: southern slope of Lago Norte, 3 km NNW of Lago Norte, Aisén Basin, Patagonia, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: 12 m thick rhyolitic ignimbrite of the Lago Norte Vocanic Complex, overlying a 50 m thick fossiliferous marine succession of Toqui Fm intercalated in the Ibáñez Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 14 (of 19) spot analyses analyzed by SHRIMP II (ANU), using the TEMORA zircon standard.
Biostratigraphy: Ammonites (Groebericeras Leanza and Blandfordiceras Cossman) from the underlying Toqui Formation, the basal unit of the Coihaique Group, indicate early Berriasian and late Berriasian ages.

Locality: Outcrops on south side of Grindstone Creek, west of State Road 306, Glen County, Great Valley, California, USA
Lithostratigraphy: Great Valley Group

Biostratigraphy: upper Argentiniceras noduliferum regional ammonite zone; within Calpionella Zone (calpionellids); therefore, upper Berriasian (Kietzmann et al., 2018).

Locality: Las Loicas; Neuquén Basin, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: Vaca Muerta Fm; ca.56m level in section

Locality: Las Loicas; Neuquén Basin, Argentina

Locality: Las Loicas; Neuquén Basin, Argentina

Biostratigraphy: uppermost Substeueroceras koeneni regional ammonite zone; uppermost Crassicollaria Zone (calpionellids); above FO nannofossil Rhadodiscus as per, below FO Nannoconus wintereri; therefore, middle Berriasian (Kietzmann et al., 2018).

Locality: Mazatepec, Puebla State; Sierra Madre, Mexico
Lithostratigraphy: Lower Tamaulipas Fm of gray limestone (lower part); ca. 23 m level in section.

Biostratigraphy: lower Calpionella elliptica subzone; above FO Nannoconus kamptneri minor, below N. steinmannii steinmanni FO; therefore, middle Berriasian (Kietzmann et al., 2018).

Locality: Las Loicas; northern Neuquén Basin, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: Vaca Muerta Fm; ca. 3 m level in section
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of three single zircon grains, utilizing CA-TIMS and the ET2535 or ET535 spike
Zone: middle(?) B. koeneni Zone, lower(?) Crassicollaria zone; projected as lower Chron M18r
Biostratigraphy: middle (?) Substeueroceras koeneni regional ammonite zone (base not exposed); within lower (?) Crassicollaria Zone (calpionellids); below FO nannofossil Umbria granulosa; therefore, middle Berriasian (Kietzmann et al., 2018).

Locality: ODP Hole 1213B (Leg 198) on Shatsky Rise, northwest Pacific
Lithostratigraphy: Lithologic Unit IV. Whole-rock=Core 28R-2 (1–6 cm) and 30R-3 (1–6 cm). Feldspars from Core 33R-3 (115–120 cm)
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of whole rock (middle sill), and plagioclase (lower sill) incremental heating plateau ages, originally calculated with FCT biotite=28.03 Ma as the fluence monitor.
Zone: Younger than NK1 nanno zone of earliest Berriasian
Biostratigraphy: Sills (reversely magnetized) were injected into sediments with Calcareous nannofossil zone NK1 and radiolarian zone Pseudodictryomitra carpatica of earliest Berriasian=. emplacement of Sills must be younger than earliest Berriasian; and perhaps during Chron M18r.

Locality: Las Loicas; northern Neuquén Basin, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: Base of Vaca Muerta Fm overlying non-marine Tordillo Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of youngest four (of seven) single zircon grains, utilizing CA-TIMS and the ET2535 or ET535 spike
Biostratigraphy: In Virgatosphinctes andesensis (same as Virg. mendozanus in some scales) regional ammonnite zone (base of ammonite recovery at this level of facies change); therefore lowermost Tithonian (Kietzmann et al., 2018)

Locality: Flodigarry, Staffin Bay, Isle of Skye, U.K.=proposed GSSP for base-Oxfordian
Lithostratigraphy: Bed 35, which is 1.30±0.1 m below Concretion-rich marker Bed 36, and near the proposed GSSP level (1.25 m below Bed 36); Flodigarry Shale Member, Staffin Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Model 3 isochron age from 9 rock powder aliquots 1( 1 replicate) sampling a of 10 cm of section, dissolved via CrVI-H2SO4.
Biostratigraphy: “subboreal Oxfordian-Kimmeridgian (Pseudocordata/ Baylei zones) boundary is placed between 1.65–1.47 m and 1.08 m below bed 36—the last occurrence of Ringsteadia and the first occurrence of Pictonia, respectively. Bed 35 is rich in Pictonia densicostata.

Locality: Kaberlaba section, in the Altopiano di Asiago (Trentino Alto Adige and Veneto regions, Italy
Lithostratigraphy: Top of middle unit (RAM) of Rosso Ammonitico
Primary radioisotopic age details: Plateau of 100% of gas released by step-heating of sanidine separate, originally calibrated to joint optimization scheme of Renne et al. (2011).
Zone: Gregoryceras transversarium ammonite zone or younger
Biostratigraphy: ammonites “chacteristic of the Gregoryceras transversarium Biozone, indicates a Middle Oxfordian age for the top of the RAM unit”; and overying upper Rosso Ammon.

Locality: 6.5 km southwest of Diagonal Mountain, central Bowser Basin, British Columbia
Lithostratigraphy: upper Hazelton Group, 45 m below the base of the Bowser Lake Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Seven multi-grain zircon fractions combined to yield a weighted mean 206Pb/238U age, utilizing air abrasion and an in-house tracer calibration
Zone: Quenstedtoceras lamberti or Q. mariae zones
Biostratigraphy: Upper Hazelton Group contains Quenstedtoceras or earliest Cardioceras of latest Callovian (Quenstedtoceras lamberti Zone) or earliest Oxfordian age (Q. mariae Zone), 45 m below the base of the Bowser Lake Group.

Locality: Chacay Melehué, Neuquén Basin, western Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: “Boundary tuff”; Los Molles Fm
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 6 (of 9) single zircon grains, utilizing CA-TIMS and the ET535 spike
Zone: Clydoniceras discus–R. anceps ammonite zone interval?
Biostratigraphy: Tuff between L. steinmanni and vergarensis regional ammonite zones. Top of local Lilloettia steinmanni ammonite assemblage zone. “A precise age cannot be established. ... Only the overling Hecticoceras proximum Zone [which is above a local Neuqueniceras bodenbenderi assemblage zone] is chararacterised by an association of Tethyan Oppeliidae indicating the latest early Callovian (Riccardi et al., 1989).”

Locality: ODP Site 801, Pigafetta basin, western Pacific; marine magnetic anomaly M43r (or M42n.4r on revised deep-tow nomenclature)
Lithostratigraphy: Tholeiitic basalts (ca. 750 mbsf; this unit extends from ca. 500 mbsf to base of hole at ca. 950 mbsf), oceanic thoeiitic basalt crystalline groundmass
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of two laser incremental heating plateau ages (41%–57% of gas) on acid-leached crystalline groundmass, originally calibrated to FCT-3 biotite=28.04 Ma.
Biostratigraphy: Probably the lower massive tholeiitic basalt is mid-Bajocian to early Bathonian [disputed, see Jurassic text; with a much older Early Bajocian or early Aalenian proposed by Bartolini and Larson (2001)]. Important constraint on Jurassic portion (Bajocian-Oxfordian) of M-sequence.

Locality: near top of Gunlock section, Washington County, Utah, USA
Lithostratigraphy: Crystal Creek Member, Carmel Fm, Utah, USA
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of six single-grain sanidine laser fusion analyses, originally using FCs = 27.84 Ma as fluence monitor.
Zone: W. laeviuscula–G. garantiana ammonite zone interval
Biostratigraphy: Bivalve correlation of Carmel Formation to ammonite-bearing Twin Creek Formation indicates an age of late Early to early Late Bajocian

Locality: near bottom of Gunlock section, Washington County, Utah, USA
Lithostratigraphy: uppermost Temple Cap Fm, Utah, USA

Locality: Eskay rhyolite east, Eskay Creek gold mine, Kitimat-Stikine A, Iskut River map area, NW British Columbia
Lithostratigraphy: Salmon River Fm, Hazelton Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of 5 multi-grain zircon fractions, utilizing physical abrasion and in-house UBC spike (0.1% error in tracer calibration). Analytical error expanded in accommodate geologic scatter.
Zone: uppermost Toarcian–mid-upper Aalenian (D. pseudoradiosa–B. bradfordensis zone interval)
Biostratigraphy: Flow-banded rhyolite is overlain by Upper Aalenian strata, correlated to Erycitoides cf. howelli ammonite zone of western North America zonation) [therefore, could be Lower Aalenian or older?]

Locality: Palquilla section near Tacna in southern Peru.
Lithostratigraphy: Pelado Formation
Primary radioisotopic age details: Weighted mean of youngest three (of six) single zircon grains, utilizing CA-TIMS and the ET535 spike
Biostratigraphy: Above strata containing Yakounia ammonites, interpreted as equivalent to Gr. thouarsense Standard Zone
Reference: Sell et al. (2014); Al-Suwaidi et al. (2016)

Locality: Yakoun River, Queen Charlotte Islands, British Columbia
Lithostratigraphy: Whiteaves Fm

Zone: upper Hild. bifrons to lower Haugia variabilis
Biostratigraphy: North American Crassicosta ammonite zone is interpreted to correlate to the upper Hild. bifrons–lower Haugia variabilis ammonite zones of NW Europe
Reference: Pálfy et al. (1997); Al-Suwaidi et al. (2016)

Locality: Serrucho Creek, west of Malargüe city, Mendoza prov., Neuquén Basin, Argentina
Lithostratigraphy: Upper tuff bed within 19.5-m-thick organic-rich shale of lower Tres Esquinas Fm (21.9 mab in measured section).

Zone: Hild. bifrons to H. variabilis Zone
Biostratigraphy: Andean Dact. hoelderi Zone to P. pacificum Zone is interpreted to be equivalent to a range from the Harp. serpentinum to Hild. bifrons Standard Zones
Reference: Mazzini et al. (2010); Al-Suwaidi et al. (2016)

Locality: Serrucho Creek, west of Malargüe city, Mendoza prov., Neuquén Basin, Argentina

Reference: Leanza et al. (2013); Al-Suwaidi et al. (2016)

Locality: Dormettingen Quarry, SW Germany.

Zone: Dact. tenuicostatum to Hild. bifrons zones
Biostratigraphy: Shale samples included in isochron include horizons spanning the Dact. tenuicostatum to Hild. bifrons zones

Locality: Spatsizi River map area, Stikine region, NW British Columbia, Canada
Lithostratigraphy: McEwan Creek pluton

Zone: Dact. tenuicostatum–Hild. bifrons ammonite zone interval?
Biostratigraphy: Intrudes volcanics with intercalated sediments of Early Toarcian age; pluton is perhaps co-magmatic with volcanism.

Locality: Palquilla section near Tacna in southern Peru.

Zone: Dact. tenuicostatum Zone/ Harp. serpentinum Zone boundary
Biostratigraphy: Lies above Dactylioceras kanense and below Hildaites striatus
Reference: Sell et al. (2014); Al-Suwaidi et al. (2016)

Lithostratigraphy: Telkwa Fm, Hazelton Group

Zone: late Sinemurian (O. oxynotum–E. raricostatum zone interval?)
Biostratigraphy: Sample from 100 m of epiclastic and pyroclastic strata above sediments with ammonite assemblages characteristic of Late Sinemurian Plesechioceras? harbledownense ammonite zone of western North America

Locality: Utcubamba valley, northern Peru; on fresh road section from Levanto to Maino.
Lithostratigraphy: Ash bed L-19 at ca. 130 m in their section of Aramachay Fm of Pucara Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Six (of 9) single zircon grain analyses yielded a weighted mean 206Pb/238U age, utilizing CA-TIMS and in-house UNIGE spike (0.1% error in tracer calibration).
Biostratigraphy: Within Badouxia canadensis ammonite beds, with a level with Angulaticeras genus about 8 m below and the lowest Vermiceras densicostatum and Metophioceras occurrence about 12 m above.
Reference: Schaltegger et al. (2008), Guex et al. (2012)

Locality: Utcubamba valley, northern Peru; on fresh road section from Levanto to Maino.
Lithostratigraphy: Ash bed at ca. 100 m in their section of Aramachay Fm of Pucara Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Eight single zircon grains analyzed with CA-TIMS and ET2535 spike illustrate excess scatter attributed to a range of growth histories prior to eruption; the authors estimate the eruption age from youngest robust grain analysis.
Biostratigraphy: In upper part of local occurrence of ammonite Kammerkarites (middle Hettangian); equivalent to Saxoceras zone in NW Europe scale.

Locality: Utcubamba valley, northern Peru; on fresh road section from Levanto to Maino.
Lithostratigraphy: Ash bed at ca. 77 m in their section of Aramachay Fm of Pucara Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Seven single zircon grains analyzed with CA-TIMS and ET2535 spike illustrate excess scatter attributed to a range of growth histories prior to eruption; the authors estimate the eruption age from youngest robust grain analysis.
Biostratigraphy: At the local lowest occurrence of ammonite Psiloceras tilmanni (early Hettangian)

Locality: Utcubamba valley, northern Peru; on fresh road section from Levanto to Maino.
Lithostratigraphy: Ash bed at ca. 68 m in their section, approximately 5 1/2 m above sample LM4-90, in Aramachay Fm of Pucara Group
Primary radioisotopic age details: Fourteen single zircon grains analyzed with CA-TIMS and ET2535 spike illustrate excess scatter attributed to a range of growth histories prior to eruption; originally published as 201.29±0.19/0.28; then revised in Wotzlaw et al. (2014b) as 201.32±0.13 Ma.
Biostratigraphy: ca. 2.5 m above lowest occurrence of Hettangian genus Psiloceras (Psiloceras spelae); which is presumed to be equivalent to the base-Jurassic GSSP level in Austria.
Reference: Schoene et al. (2010); Wotzlaw et al. (2014b)

Locality: New York Canyon, Nevada, USA
Lithostratigraphy: New York Canyon section [stratigraphy, ammonites, carbon-isotopes in Guex et al. (2004)]; which was candidate for base-Triassic GSSP.
Primary radioisotopic age details: Seventeen single zircon grains analyzed with CA-TIMS and ET2535 spike. Estimate of eruption age from youngest robust grain at 201.33±0.19 Ma; weighted mean of 9 youngest robust grains is statistically equivalent at 201.45±0.12 Ma.
Biostratigraphy: 1.5 m above the lowest occurrence of Hettangian genus Psiloceras (Psiloceras spelae); which is presumed to be equivalent to the base-Jurassic GSSP level in Austria.
Reference: Schoene et al. (2010); Wotzlaw et al. (2014b)

Locality: Utcubamba valley, northern Peru; on fresh road section from Levanto to Maino.
Lithostratigraphy: Ash bed 90 at ca. 65 m in their section of Aramachay Fm of Pucara Group.
Primary radioisotopic age details: Fourteen single zircon grains analyzed with CA-TIMS and ET2535 spike include Proterozoic xenocrysts, a cluster of 9 equivalent grains and one young analysis attributed to Pb-loss; the authors estimate the eruption age from most precise, young, robust grain, although a weighted mean of nine grains is statistically equivalent.
Biostratigraphy: Mid-way between highest local occurrence of the topmost Triassic ammonite genus Choristoceras (Choristo. crickmayi, 3 m below) and lowest occurrence of Hettangian genus Psiloceras (Psiloceras spelae, about 3 m higher)=. middle of “extinction interval” of end-Triassic. Tri/Jur boundary projected as about the 64 m level in section (FAD of Psiloceras spelae).
Reference: Schoene et al. (2010); Wotzlaw et al. (2014b)

Locality: Utcubamba valley, northern Peru; on fresh road section from Levanto to Maino.
Lithostratigraphy: Ash bed 86 at ca. 59 m level in their section of Aramachay Fm of Pucara Group.
Primary radioisotopic age details: Fourteen single zircon grains analyzed with CA-TIMS and ET2535 spike illustrate excess scatter; the authors estimate the eruption age from youngest robust grain, although a weighted mean of youngest three robust grains is statistically equivalent.
Biostratigraphy: One meter above the highest local occurrence of the topmost Triassic ammonite genus Choristoceras (Choristo. crickmayi, in Bed 84b, 59.5 m level), and 5 m below the Hettangian genus Psiloceras (Psiloceras spelae, in bed 93b, 64.5 m level) and about 18 m below Psiloceras tilmanni (Bed 114-129, lowest at 77.5 m level).
Reference: Schoene et al. (2010); Wotzlaw et al. (2014b)

Locality: Utcubamba valley, northern Peru; on fresh road section from Levanto to Maino.
Lithostratigraphy: Ash bed at ca. 51 m level in their section of Aramachay Fm of Pucara Group.
Primary radioisotopic age details: Utilizing CA-TIMS and in-house UNIGE spike (0.1% error in tracer calibration). Originally published as 201.78±0.16 in Guex et al. (2012); then revised by them in Wotzlaw et al. (2014b) as 201.87±0.17 Ma.
Biostratigraphy: Between Vandaites saximontanum (mid-Rhaetian) and Choristoceras crickmayi (late Rhaetian)
Reference: Guex et al. (2012); Wotzlaw et al. (2014b)

Locality: Utcubamba valley, northern Peru; on fresh road section from Levanto to Maino.

Mid-Upper Carnian is suggested by “Lower Carnian conodonts (Glad. spp., N. postkockeli, P. inclinata, P. tadpole) abruptly disappear 3 m below the ash bed at a level corresponding to the Carnian pluvial event” and “Carnian-Norian boundary can be placed 6 m above the ash bed with the first occurrence of M. communisti.”
